goldens.query: How do I create a quiz?
goldens.expected_output: To create a quiz, go to the Dashboard in the sidebar and click the Create Exam quick action card or press Ctrl+K (or Cmd+K) and type "Create Exam" to open the creation wizard at the /quizzes/create page. Next, enter your exam title, add your source content by pasting text, uploading files, or entering URLs, and choose your AI generation mode. Finally, click the Generate button at the bottom of the wizard to produce your questions.

goldens.query: Where is Monitoring in the sidebar?
goldens.expected_output: Monitoring is not located in the sidebar. To find it, click Exams in the left sidebar, open the specific exam card, and then select the Monitoring tab.

goldens.query: How do I publish my exam?
goldens.expected_output: To publish your exam, first ensure every question shows a green Approved badge on the Questions tab. Next, click Exams in the left sidebar and open your exam workspace by clicking your exam card. Finally, click the prominent emerald-green Publish button located on the exam card or at the top of the exam workspace view.

goldens.query: What is verification schema before an exam?
goldens.expected_output: Verification Schema is the identity form students fill out before starting an exam to collect details like their name, enrollment number, class, or batch. It is the first thing students interact with to establish who they are, but it is not related to answer grading or scoring rules. Teachers configure it by clicking **Exams**, selecting an exam card, opening the **Settings** tab, and expanding the **Verification Schema** section.

goldens.query: How do I host an Arena battle with a room code?
goldens.expected_output: To host an Arena battle, click Arena in the left sidebar and select or create an approved quiz pack. Configure your battle settings, then click the emerald-green Create Room button to generate a six-character room code and join URL. Share the code, link, or QR code with players, wait for them to join the lobby, and click the emerald-green Start button to begin.

goldens.query: Connect Google Classroom and push grades
goldens.expected_output: Scores are automatically pushed back to the Google Classroom coursework entry after a student submits and grading completes. Teachers can also trigger a manual grade push from the Classroom section in Integrations.

goldens.query: Why is Analytics empty with no data?
goldens.expected_output: Analytics is empty when no exams have graded results yet. To fix this, verify that your date range filter is not too narrow. Then check that exams have been published, students have taken and submitted them, and grading has completed. Publishing alone does not populate Analytics.

goldens.query: How does grading work for short answers?
goldens.expected_output: Short answer questions go through a layered smart grading pipeline that combines exact matching, fuzzy matching, keyword analysis, embedding similarity, and AI evaluation. Each layer attempts to resolve the answer before escalating to the next step, and if confidence remains too low, it is marked as "Pending Professor Review" for manual scoring by the teacher.

goldens.query: Export results to CSV or Excel
goldens.expected_output: In the left sidebar, click Exams and select the exam card, then click the Results tab at the top of the workspace. Click the Export button (or dropdown menu) in the top-right area of the Results tab and choose your format, such as CSV or Excel. A background job starts, and you will receive an in-app notification with a download link once it is ready.

goldens.query: What exam settings control time limits?
goldens.expected_output: To set exam time limits, go to Exams (sidebar), open the exam, and select the Settings tab. Near the top of the Settings page, find the Duration field to change how long each student has (default is 60 minutes, with a minimum of 5 minutes).

goldens.query: How do students take an exam from a link?
goldens.expected_output: Students click the published exam link shared by the teacher to open the start page in their web browser. Next, they read the exam info, fill out the identity verification form (and enter an access code if required), and click the Start Exam button. After granting any necessary browser permissions for fullscreen or webcam access, they answer the questions in the exam interface. Finally, when ready, they click the Submit button and confirm to complete the exam.

goldens.query: Question types MCQ and true false
goldens.expected_output: Multiple Choice (MCQ) presents a set of answer options where exactly one is correct and is graded instantly by comparing to the correct option. True/False is a binary choice question where the student selects True or False and is graded instantly by comparing to the correct answer. Both MCQ and True/False question cards show their question type as a small badge on the Questions tab in the exam workspace.

goldens.query: What is Quizzer and who is it for?
goldens.expected_output: Quizzer is an AI-powered assessment platform for creating, delivering, monitoring, and analyzing exams. It is built for anyone who needs to build assessments—ranging from students practicing on their own to solo teachers, tutors, trainers, freelancers, teams, startups, coaching institutes, schools, universities, HR professionals, and content creators.

goldens.query: Difference between Monitoring and Analytics
goldens.expected_output: Monitoring is a tab located inside each individual exam workspace that shows real-time data for in-progress and completed attempts. In contrast, Analytics is a sidebar workspace that shows aggregate performance data, trends, and charts across multiple exams.

goldens.query: Teacher vs student role permissions
goldens.expected_output: Teachers have full access to the sidebar workspaces (Dashboard, Exams, Arena, Students, Analytics, Integrations), exam workspace tabs, and account settings, allowing them to create and manage assessments. In contrast, students who select the Student persona during onboarding receive a deliberately limited interface and cannot access the Exams workspace, Arena hosting, Analytics, or teacher tools. Students enter exams exclusively through shared links, while exam takers without an account only interact with a separate, focused exam interface using a verification form and attempt token.

goldens.query: Students workspace cohort health
goldens.expected_output: To access information about cohort health, open the Students workspace by clicking Students in the left sidebar. Below the scope bar, check the metrics strip, which includes a "Cohort count" card showing the number of distinct cohorts or groups. Additionally, a cohort health visualization displays the distribution of readiness across the student population to provide a snapshot of overall performance.

goldens.query: Schedule exam on Google Calendar
goldens.expected_output: To schedule an exam, first connect Google Calendar by clicking "Integrations" in the left sidebar, finding the Google Calendar card, and clicking "Connect" to authorize Quizzer. Next, ensure your exam is published by going to "Exams" and verifying the green "Published" badge. Finally, schedule the exam either from the post-publish success screen by clicking "Schedule on Calendar," or from the "Integrations" page by clicking "Schedule Exam" and selecting the published exam from the dropdown.

goldens.query: Import source files from Google Drive
goldens.expected_output: To import source files from Google Drive, first connect Drive by clicking **Integrations** in the left sidebar, finding the Google Drive card, and clicking **Connect**. Next, start creating an exam from the Dashboard quick actions or by pressing Ctrl+K and typing "Create Exam." In the source content area's **Files tab**, click the **Import from Google Drive** button, browse or search for your file, and click **Select or Import**.

goldens.query: How does onboarding work after signup?
goldens.expected_output: After signing up, you complete a four-step onboarding flow where you enter your display name, choose a persona from a grid of ten options, and optionally fill in details like your institution or subject area. Finally, a celebration animation plays while your workspace is set up, after which you are automatically redirected to your dashboard.

goldens.query: Change account settings and profile
goldens.expected_output: To manage your profile and account settings, open the left sidebar, go to the **ACCOUNT** section, and click **Settings** (or use the command palette with Ctrl+K / Cmd+K). Account Settings is organized into tabbed sections including Profile, Preferences, Workspace, Security, and Notifications. In the Profile tab, you can update your display name, phone number, institution, country, timezone, subject area, courses taught, teaching experience, professional title, and avatar.

goldens.query: How do I send feedback about Quizzer?
goldens.expected_output: On desktop, scroll to the **ACCOUNT** section in the left sidebar and click **Send feedback** to open the `/feedback` page. On mobile, open the account or more menu from the bottom navigation and tap **Send feedback**.

goldens.query: Notification preferences and email
goldens.expected_output: To change which notifications you receive, go to Account Settings via sidebar ACCOUNT, select **Settings**, and click the Notifications tab to toggle switches on or off. Quizzer does not send email notifications for events like exam generation, student attempts, integrity alerts, or export readiness, as these are in-app only. Email is used exclusively for signup email verification, password resets, and exam share invitations.

goldens.query: What shows on the teacher dashboard?
goldens.expected_output: The teacher dashboard shows four summary metric cards (Active Right Now, Attempts (7d), Avg Score (7d), and AI Jobs Running), a live exams panel with currently active attempts, and quick actions for common tasks like creating an exam. For newer accounts, it also displays a dismissible activation checklist guiding first steps.

goldens.query: Exam lifecycle draft published archived
goldens.expected_output: An exam exists in three lifecycle states: Draft (being prepared and not accessible to students), Published (live and accessible via share link), and Archived (retired with no new attempts, but results preserved). You can transition an exam from Draft to Published using the canonical click path `exam.publish` (approve all questions, then click **Publish**). To archive an exam when it is finished, click the Archive action on the exam card in the Exams workspace.

goldens.query: Common workflow create exam then share link
goldens.expected_output: To create an exam and share the link, open Create Exam from the Dashboard or press Ctrl+K and type "Create Exam," then add your content, select a generation mode, and click Generate. Review and approve the questions in the Questions tab, configure your preferences in the Settings tab, and click the emerald-green Publish button. Finally, click Copy Link on the success screen or find the URL on the Links tab to send it to students.

goldens.query: Generation failed or daily AI quota
goldens.expected_output: If AI generation failed, check the notification for error details. Common causes include source documents that were too short, content that could not be extracted (such as a corrupted or image-only PDF), or a temporary AI service error. Try again with different source content or split a large document into smaller sections. If you have exhausted your daily AI generation quota, wait until the next day, as the quota resets daily.

goldens.query: Integrity events and live proctoring
goldens.expected_output: To view integrity events for a live proctored exam, click **Exams** in the left sidebar, select the specific exam card showing the LIVE badge, and click the **Monitoring** tab. From there, click on a specific attempt row to expand it and view the chronological timeline of integrity events, such as tab switches, fullscreen exits, phone detections, and face checks.

goldens.query: Approve draft questions before publish
goldens.expected_output: To approve draft questions before publishing, open your exam from the Exams workspace in the left sidebar and select the **Questions tab**. Review each question card and click the **Approve** button (checkmark icon or green action) to mark it as ready, or use the **Bulk Approve** action at the top of the list to approve all remaining Draft questions at once. All questions must be in Approved status before you can publish the exam.

goldens.query: Negative marking settings
goldens.expected_output: When negative marking is enabled in the exam settings, correct answers receive full marks, wrong answers result in a configured penalty deduction, and unanswered questions receive no marks and no penalty. The penalty amount is set per exam using the Penalty for Wrong Answer setting, and negative marking applies to all question types.

goldens.query: Command palette and sidebar navigation
goldens.expected_output: Press Ctrl+K (Windows) or Cmd+K (Mac) to open the command palette, a search overlay used to quickly jump to any workspace, search exams, or trigger actions. To navigate the sidebar, click Exams on the left side of the screen to view your exam library as cards, then click any exam card to open its workspace. At the top of the exam workspace, a tab row appears allowing you to switch between Questions, Monitoring, Results, Links, and Settings.

goldens.query: Link window vs exam duration meaning
goldens.expected_output: Link window controls when students can begin by defining how long the published link accepts new starts (measured in hours or days). Duration is the per-attempt timer that controls how long students can work once they begin (measured in minutes). For example, a 60-minute exam with a 24-hour link window means students have 24 hours to start and 60 minutes once they start.

goldens.query: Join Arena as a player with code
goldens.expected_output: Players open the join link or go to the Arena join page and enter the room code manually. They choose a unique nickname consisting of 2 to 20 characters (alphanumeric plus spaces, underscores, and hyphens). Alternatively, if the host linked a Google Classroom course, players can pick from the class roster instead of typing a nickname. No Quizzer account is required.

goldens.query: Results tab integrity review
goldens.expected_output: To view integrity details, click on any result row in the Results tab to expand it. The Integrity Review Panel opens below, showing a chronological violation timeline and aggregated violation buckets.

goldens.query: Cannot publish questions stuck in draft
goldens.expected_output: To publish an exam, every question must be in Approved status, as Draft or Rejected questions will block publishing. Open your exam from the Exams workspace, click the Questions tab, and review your questions. Click the Approve button on each question card, or use the Bulk Approve action to change all remaining Draft questions to Approved.

goldens.query: What is the weather in Paris today?
I want to make a test for my class from my PDF notes

Enter your exam title, then upload your PDF file in the source content panel by dragging and dropping it or using the file selector. Choose an AI generation mode (such as Source-first or Guided) and click the Generate button. Finally, open the exam from the Exams list, review your questions under the Questions tab, and publish when ready.

goldens.query: how do I put my quiz online so students can attempt it
goldens.expected_output: To put your quiz online, first open your exam workspace by clicking "Exams" in the left sidebar and selecting your exam card. Go to the Questions tab to verify that every question shows a green "Approved" badge, approving any remaining Draft or Rejected questions. Next, click the prominent emerald-green "Publish" button located on the exam card or at the top of the exam workspace. Finally, copy the generated exam URL from the success screen or the Links tab to share the link with your students.

goldens.query: give students the link to the exam
goldens.expected_output: After publishing your exam, you can find and copy the share link from the post-publish success screen, the Exams workspace, or the Links tab inside the exam workspace. You can share this link with students by copying and pasting it into any messaging app, email client, or LMS, sharing it by email from the Links tab (for up to 50 recipients), assigning it as coursework via Google Classroom, or generating a scannable QR code.

goldens.query: download my students' marks sheet
goldens.expected_output: To download your students' marks, click Exams in the left sidebar and select the specific exam. At the top of the exam workspace, click the Results tab, then click the Export button (usually in the top-right area). Choose your format—CSV, Excel, or Google Sheets—to start a background job. Once ready, you will receive an in-app notification via the bell icon in the top bar containing your download link.

goldens.query: how are written answers scored
goldens.expected_output:
Written answers (Short Answer and Long Answer) go through a layered grading pipeline. 
Step 1 is exact match after normalization, awarding full marks immediately if correct. 
Step 2 uses fuzzy match for short strings to catch minor typos. 
Step 3 checks keyword overlap for essential concepts, and Step 4 applies embedding similarity for semantic comparison. 
Step 5 uses a batched AI model if previous steps cannot score it, and Step 6 marks it as "Pending Professor Review" for manual grading if AI confidence is too low.

goldens.query: stop students from switching tabs during the test
goldens.expected_output: To stop students from switching tabs during a test, open Exams from the left sidebar and click on your exam card to open the workspace. Click the Settings tab at the top of the workspace, and scroll down to the Proctoring and Integrity section. Ensure the "Block Tab Switching" toggle switch is turned on, as it is enabled by default to detect when students leave the exam tab. Settings auto-save as you make changes.

goldens.query: play a live quiz game with my class
goldens.expected_output: To play a live quiz game with your class, go to Arena in the left sidebar and select or create an approved quiz pack. Configure your battle settings, click Create Room to generate a six-character code and join URL, and project the room screen so students can see it. Share the code with your players so they can join the lobby with a nickname, and click Start when you are ready. You can then control the game flow using the Reveal, Next, Skip, Pause, and End buttons while students answer questions in real time.

goldens.query: sync my scores to Google Classroom
goldens.expected_output: Scores are automatically synced back to the Google Classroom coursework entry after students take the exam and grading completes. Teachers can also trigger a manual grade push from the Classroom section in Integrations.

goldens.query: put the exam date in my calendar
goldens.expected_output: To put the exam date in your calendar, first make sure your exam is published and your Google Calendar is connected under Integrations in the left sidebar. Then, schedule the exam either by clicking "Schedule on Calendar" from the post-publish success screen or by going to the Integrations page, finding the Calendar section, and clicking "Schedule Exam" while selecting your published exam from the dropdown. Finally, choose the date and time for the event and click "Schedule" to create the calendar event on your primary Google Calendar.

goldens.query: can students retake the exam
goldens.expected_output: Yes, students can retake the exam if the teacher sets the Maximum Attempts option to a number greater than 1 in the exam settings. Each retake is a fully independent attempt with its own timer, answers, and violation record. To take another attempt, the student opens the same shared exam link again and is identified by their verification fields.

goldens.query: what happens to my exam when I archive it
goldens.expected_output: When you archive an exam, it is retired so that students cannot start new attempts, and its share link is deactivated. All existing results are preserved and remain accessible in the Results tab. Additionally, archived exams can later be unarchived.

goldens.query: see who is cheating right now
goldens.expected_output: To see who is cheating or taking an exam right now, click **Exams** in the left sidebar and look for exam cards with a pulsing **LIVE** badge. Alternatively, you can view the **Live Exams panel** on the Dashboard for a quick overview across all exams. Click on an active exam card and select the **Monitoring tab**, where you will see a table of in-progress attempts showing student names, violation counts, and attempt statuses. Click on a specific attempt row to expand the integrity detail panel and view a real-time, chronological timeline of events like tab switches, fullscreen exits, and phone detections as they happen.

goldens.query: publsh exam

Once published, a success screen will appear providing the unique shareable exam link.

Preferences Tab
## Preferences Tab
Theme: choose Light, Dark, or System (follows your device setting).
Default: System.

Density: Comfortable (more spacing) or Compact (denser layout).
Default: Comfortable.

Motion: System (follows device accessibility setting), Reduce (minimal
animations), or Allow (full animations). Default: System.

Time format: 12-hour or 24-hour clock. Default: 12-hour.

Live data refresh: control whether live data (like LIVE badges and
monitoring) refreshes automatically. Default: on.

Sidebar collapsed: whether the sidebar starts collapsed. Default: off.

Students scope default: the default scope mode for the Students
workspace — All in cluster or Pick exams. Default: varies.

Highlight integrity risks: whether to visually emphasize integrity-
flagged items. Default: on.

Preferences are saved locally in your browser (localStorage). They do
not sync across devices.

source_context:
Step-by-Step UI Guide: Using Analytics
## Step-by-Step UI Guide: Using Analytics
Step 1 — Open Analytics:
In the left sidebar, click Analytics (it has a chart icon). The
Analytics workspace loads showing your aggregate data.

Step 2 — Check the date range:
At the top of the Analytics page, find the date range filter. It may
be set to a specific period (like "Last 7 days"). Click the date
picker to widen or narrow the range. This is the most common reason
Analytics appears empty — the date range might not include your data.

Step 3 — Read the summary metrics:
At the top, you will see metric cards showing: Total attempts,
Completion rate, Average score, Score spread, and Integrity flags.
Each card shows the current value and a comparison to the previous

goldens.query: How do I set up webcam monitoring and auto-submit for a proctored exam?
goldens.expected_output: To set up webcam monitoring and auto-submit, go to the Settings tab in the exam workspace under the Proctoring section, toggle on Enable Webcam Monitoring (and configure Phone Detection or Face Monitoring as needed), set the Violation Limit, and toggle on Enable Auto-Submit.
source_context:
Run a Proctored Exam
1. Create an exam and generate questions (see workflow above).
2. Click the Settings tab in the exam workspace. Scroll to the
   Proctoring section.
3. Verify these toggles are on (green): Require Fullscreen, Block Tab
   Switching, Block Copy/Paste. They are on by default.
4. Toggle on Enable Webcam Monitoring. Additional webcam settings
   appear below: Phone Detection (on by default), Face Monitoring
   (toggle on if you want face presence checks).
5. Set the Violation Limit field (default 3) to your desired threshold.
6. Toggle on Enable Auto-Submit if you want the exam to end
   automatically when the limit is reached.
7. Set Duration to the appropriate time for your exam.
8. Expand Verification Schema and configure identity fields (name,
   enrollment number, etc.) using a preset or custom fields.
9. Click Publish (emerald-green button).
10. Share the link. During the exam, click Exams in the sidebar, open
    the exam, and click the Monitoring tab to watch integrity events
    in real time.
11. After students submit, click the Results tab. Look for the
    integrity flag column and expand flagged rows to see violation
    timelines.

goldens.query: How do I get better AI-generated questions in Quizzer?
goldens.expected_output: Provide clear, well-structured source content with organized material, clear topics, and concepts.
source_context:
Tips for Better AI Generation
## Tips for Better AI Generation
Provide clear, well-structured source content. The AI generates better
questions from organized material with clear topics and concepts.

Use Guided mode when you need exact control. Source-first is convenient
but may not match your exact expectations for question count or type.

For best OCR results on scanned PDFs, ensure the scan is clean and
text is legible. Blurry or low-resolution scans produce poor text
extraction.

YouTube URLs work best when the video has good captions (manual or
auto-generated). Videos with poor audio or no captions may not produce
useful text.

Splitting very large documents across multiple exams can produce better
results than feeding everything into one generation.

What Makes the Dashboard Empty
## What Makes the Dashboard Empty
The teacher dashboard may show an empty or minimal state when:
- No exams have been created yet (the activation checklist guides you)
- No exams have LIVE activity

source_context:
Common Questions
## Common Questions
Why is everything empty when I just signed up?
You need to create an exam first. Everything downstream depends on
having exams with published content and student submissions.

I published my exam but Analytics is still empty. Why?
Publishing is step 1. Students need to take the exam and submit it.
After grading completes, Analytics will show data. Also check your
date range filter.

I imported my Classroom roster but Students workspace is empty:
Roster import brings names, not attempt data. Students must actually
take exams for scores and readiness to appear.

goldens.query: How do I change my exam settings after it's already been published?
goldens.expected_output: Most settings can be changed on a published exam, but they generally only affect future attempts and do not change in-progress ones. Finalize settings before publishing when possible, as changes only impact students who start a new attempt after the change.
source_context:
Settings After Publishing
## Settings After Publishing
Most settings can be changed on a published exam. Key considerations:

Timer changes: affect future attempts only, not in-progress ones.
Students who already started keep their original timer.

Proctoring changes: affect future attempts. In-progress attempts use
the proctoring settings from when they started.

Question changes: correct answer edits do not affect frozen answer
keys in existing attempts. New questions appear in future attempts.

Attempt limit changes: may allow or restrict additional attempts for
students who have already taken the exam.

Shuffle changes: affect future attempts only.

Verification schema changes: affect future attempts. Already-submitted
verification data is not modified.

Best practice: finalize settings before publishing. If changes are
needed on a live exam, be aware that they only affect students who
start a new attempt after the change.

goldens.query: How do I connect Google Classroom to Quizzer?
goldens.expected_output: Go to Integrations in the sidebar, find Google Classroom, click Connect, and complete the Google OAuth authorization.
source_context:
Common Questions
## Common Questions
How do I connect Google Classroom?
Go to Integrations in the sidebar, find Google Classroom, and click
Connect. Complete the Google OAuth authorization.

How do I import my class roster?
After connecting, go to the Classroom section in Integrations, import
your courses, then import the roster for a specific course.

How do I assign an exam to my Classroom students?
Publish your exam first, then use the Classroom section to create a
coursework entry linking to your exam. Students see it in their
Google Classroom.

Are grades synced automatically?
Yes. After a student submits and grading completes, scores are
automatically pushed to Classroom. You can also trigger a manual push.

Does importing the roster mean students have taken the exam?
No. Roster import brings in names from Google Classroom enrollment.
Students must actually open the exam link and take the exam for
attempt data and scores to appear.

Can I use Classroom sign-in to connect?
No. Classroom uses a separate OAuth connection from Google Sign-In.
You connect Classroom through the Integrations page, not through
your login.

goldens.query: How do I change how short answer questions are graded in my exam settings?
goldens.expected_output: Use the Answer Grading Style setting on the exam's Settings tab to control how written answers are evaluated.
source_context:
Grading Style
## Grading Style
The Answer Grading Style setting on the exam's Settings tab controls
how written answers are evaluated. It only appears when the exam has
Short Answer or Long Answer questions.

Balanced: standard evaluation considering correctness, completeness,
and clarity. Good for most subjects.

Writing and Language: emphasizes grammar, structure, expression, and
language quality. Best for language arts, literature, and writing exams.

Formulas and STEM: emphasizes mathematical notation, formulas, units,
and scientific accuracy. Best for math, physics, chemistry, and
engineering exams.

Ideas and Concepts: emphasizes conceptual understanding and reasoning
over exact wording. Best for social sciences, philosophy, and
discussion-based exams.

Key Terms: emphasizes the presence of specific technical terms and
vocabulary. Best for exams where using correct terminology matters
(medical, legal, technical fields).

Users may call this: scoring mode, marking style, evaluation method,
how to change grading.

goldens.query: How do I unpublish an exam in Quizzer without losing my results?
goldens.expected_output: Simply unpublish the exam. Results stay and remain accessible in the Results tab.
source_context:
What Happens to Results
## What Happens to Results
Results are never lost during state transitions:

Unpublish: results stay. Accessible in the Results tab.
Archive: results stay. Accessible in the Results tab.
Delete (with attempts): archives instead, results stay.
Re-publish after unpublish: results stay. New attempts can be added.

The only way to lose results is if an exam with zero attempts is
deleted (there are no results to lose in that case).

Step-by-Step UI Guide: Using Notifications
## Step-by-Step UI Guide: Using Notifications
Step 1 — Check for new notifications:
Look at the top-right corner of the screen. The bell icon shows a
number badge if you have unread notifications (for example, a red
circle with "3").

Step 2 — Open the inbox:
Click the bell icon. A dropdown panel opens showing your recent
notifications in chronological order. Each notification shows a title,
a brief description, and a timestamp.

Step 3 — Click a notification:
Click on any notification to see its details and navigate to the
relevant page. For example, clicking "Generation complete" takes you

Step 4 — Mark as read:

the inbox to clear all unread badges at once.

Step 5 — Configure preferences:

(sidebar ACCOUNT → **Settings**). Click
the Notifications tab. Toggle switches on or off for each notification
category.

goldens.query: How do I publish an exam in Quizzer?
goldens.expected_output: Open your exam from the Exams workspace, then use the Publish action found on the exam card or inside the exam workspace.
source_context:
How to Publish
## How to Publish
Open your exam from the Exams workspace, then use the Publish action.
The Publish button is available:
- On the exam card in the Exams workspace list
- Inside the exam workspace (top-level action)

On publish, the system:
- Validates all publish requirements
- Generates a unique public link (UUID-based) if this is the first
  publish
- Sets a link window based on your subscription tier
- Makes the exam accessible to students via the link
- Sends a Publish confirmation notification

After publishing, the exam's status changes from Draft to Published.

goldens.query: How do I set the correct answer for a True/False question?
goldens.expected_output: Mark one of True or False as correct.
source_context:
Correct Answers
## Correct Answers
MCQ: exactly one option must be marked as correct. The question cannot
be approved without a valid correct answer.

True/False: one of True or False must be marked as correct. Same
approval requirement.

Short Answer: one or more accepted answers can be set. The grading
pipeline uses smart matching, so minor variations (spelling differences,
extra spaces, case changes) may still match even if not explicitly
listed as accepted answers.

Long Answer: there is no single "correct answer" field. Grading uses
AI evaluation against the question context, the source material, and
the grading style setting. Teachers may set reference answers or key
points to guide the AI evaluator.

Multi-Select: one or more options must be marked as correct. All
correct options must be identified. The student must select exactly
the correct set for full marks.

goldens.query: Where can I find the exam results to download them?
goldens.expected_output: To find the exam results to download, go to the Results tab at the top of the exam workspace and look for the Export button (usually in the top-right area or as a dropdown menu).
source_context:
Step-by-Step UI Guide: Viewing and Exporting Results
## Step-by-Step UI Guide: Viewing and Exporting Results
Step 1 — Open the exam:
In the left sidebar, click Exams. Click on the exam card whose results
you want to see.

Step 2 — Go to the Results tab:
At the top of the exam workspace, click the Results tab (third tab:
Questions, Monitoring, Results, Links, Settings). The results table
loads showing all submitted attempts.

Step 3 — Read the results table:
Each row shows one submitted attempt with columns: Student name,
Enrollment number (if collected), Final score, Violation count,
Integrity flag, Status (Graded or Pending Professor Review), and
Submitted timestamp.

Step 4 — View integrity details:
Click on any result row to expand it. The Integrity Review Panel opens
below, showing a violation timeline (chronological list of all
integrity events during that attempt) and violation buckets
(categorized counts).

Step 5 — Export results:
Look for the Export button (usually in the top-right area of the
Results tab, or as a dropdown menu). Click it and choose your format:

goldens.expected_output: Sign up and select a non-student persona during onboarding to get the Teacher role.
source_context:
Teacher Role
## Teacher Role
Anyone who signs up and selects a non-student persona during onboarding
gets the Teacher role. This includes actual teachers, trainers,
freelancers, HR professionals, developers, content creators, business
team leads, self-study users, and anyone else who wants to create
assessments.

What teachers can access:

Sidebar workspaces:
- Dashboard: overview of exam activity, live exams, metrics, quick
  actions, activation checklist
- Exams: full exam library (draft, published, archived), create,
  manage, publish, share, delete
- Arena: host live quiz battles, create packs, view game history
- Students: learner directory, readiness labels, support queue, cohort
  health, CSV export
- Analytics: cross-exam performance trends, charts, Arena analytics
- Integrations: connect/manage Google Classroom, Calendar, Drive
